solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fraud dealt with by Yard after call

indicators.note: after tells us the yard letter follows the call word in the answer

parts.note: to call someone is to phone them
Y is the standard abbreviation for yard, the unit of length

explanation.surface: A con artist is being handled by Scotland Yard after a tip-off phone call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yard' suggests Scotland Yard, the London police, but it is just the unit abbreviation Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A phoney is a fake or impostor, someone who pretends to be what they are not.

clue.text: Come out quietly, then go off getting offensive

parts.note: P is piano, the musical marking for quietly
to rot is to go off or decay
rude means offensive

explanation.surface: Someone emerges quietly and then turns nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: To protrude is to stick out, which is to come out beyond a surface.

clue.text: Fantastic, a church spreading the message further afield?

parts.note: outré means bizarre or fantastic

explanation.surface: An eccentric church is evangelising beyond its own walls.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a descriptive definition rather than a dictionary synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Outreach is the work of taking a service or message to people beyond the usual audience.

clue.text: Birds stuffed in the museum

indicators.note: stuffed in means placed inside, so the letters are found within these words

explanation.surface: Stuffed birds are on display in the museum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuffed' plays on taxidermy, but it signals letters packed inside 'the museum'.
explanation.definitionFit: Emus are large flightless Australian birds.

clue.text: I'm sorry about ruler being frightening

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the apology word is read backwards

parts.note: oops is an exclamation of apology for a blunder
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: Someone apologises because the monarch has been scaring people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the apology round; 'being' is just a link joining wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Spooking means scaring or startling, the present participle matching frightening.

clue.text: Older pro gets relocated in room by front of college

indicators.note: relocated means moved to new places, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An older professional is moved into a room by the college entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' belongs to the anagram fodder, not a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A porters' lodge is the room at the gate of a college where porters keep watch.

clue.text: Conservatively minded drivers proceed thus in the UK

definitions.meaning: holding conservative political views, at the right of the spectrum

definitions.text: drivers proceed thus in the UK
definitions.meaning: describes the side on which British drivers sit and overtake

explanation.walkthrough: British cars are right-hand drive and overtake on the outside lane, the right-hand side.
explanation.definitionFit: Being of the right politically means holding conservative views.

clue.text: Book is excellent — what a surprise!

parts.note: A1 read as AI means first-class or excellent
ah is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: Someone is amazed that a book is so good.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is a common term for first-rate, written with the letter I standing for the digit.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaiah is a book of the Old Testament, named after the prophet.

clue.text: It could win the Derby? My, my!

definitions.meaning: a racehorse, in childish slang; the Derby is England's top flat horse race

explanation.walkthrough: The Derby is a famous horse race run at Epsom in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Gee-gee is nursery slang for a horse, while gee gee repeats the mild exclamation gee.

clue.text: Opening very big stomach — front of instrument goes in

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, a clothing label for very big sizes

indicators.note: goes in tells us that letter is placed inside the stomach word

parts.note: tum is an informal word for stomach

indicators.note: front of means only the opening letter of instrument is used

explanation.surface: A surgical instrument is pushed into a very large belly through an opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'front of' takes the first letter of instrument, and 'goes in' puts it inside the stomach word; OS is a clothing-size label for outsize.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostium is the anatomical term for a mouth-like opening, such as that of a duct or vessel.

clue.text: Professional guy reveals enzyme

parts.note: pro is short for professional
to guy someone is to mock or tease them

explanation.surface: A professional man discloses something about an enzyme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guy' looks like a noun for a man, but here it is the verb meaning to ridicule.
explanation.definitionFit: A protease is an enzyme that breaks down proteins.

clue.text: Protest about vessel used in Mass

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a monstrance is the vessel in which the consecrated host is displayed

explanation.surface: Someone complains about a sacred vessel used in a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: A remonstrance is a formal protest or complaint.

clue.text: Proper-sounding dance

indicators.note: sounding tells us the answer is said like the word for proper

parts.note: proper in the sense of genuine or real

explanation.surface: A dance that sounds respectable.
explanation.definitionFit: A reel is a lively Scottish or Irish folk dance.

clue.text: Editor about to make merry, with book out, and ease up

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the editor abbreviation is read backwards
out means the book letter is removed from the merrymaking word

parts.note: to celebrate is to make merry

explanation.surface: An editor is told to stop partying and stop reading, and just relax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns ED into DE; 'out' drops B from CELEBRATE to leave CELERATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To decelerate is to slow down, which is to ease up on speed.

clue.text: Fresh air — amounts needed in convalescent home

indicators.note: fresh means new, so the letters are arranged anew

explanation.surface: Patients recovering at a clinic need plenty of fresh air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh' seems to describe the air, but it signals rearranging AIR and AMOUNTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A sanatorium is an institution where people recover from illness, a convalescent home.

clue.text: I'd tip Castro to reform, limiting hard sort of regime he's had

indicators.note: limiting means enclosing, so the rearranged letters surround the hard letter
to reform means to re-form, so the letters are rearranged into a new order

parts.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A tipster bets that Castro will change his ways, despite the harsh rule he has had.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reform' rearranges IDTIPCASTRO, and 'limiting' wraps it round H. 'he' is Castro, so the definition describes his own government.
explanation.definitionFit: Fidel Castro ruled Cuba as a one-party dictator, so his regime was a dictatorship.

clue.text: Happen to meet dissolute fellow on horse

parts.note: a bum is a lazy, disreputable person
a pinto is a piebald horse

explanation.surface: Someone happens across a dissolute man riding a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: To bump into someone is an idiom for meeting them by chance.

clue.text: Mountain I've to go up carried by Tony and Hilary?

indicators.note: carried by means held inside the surname plural

parts.note: Tony Benn and his son Hilary Benn are Labour politicians, the two Benns

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the letters read upwards, backwards

explanation.surface: A climber is ready to be lifted up a mountain by two politicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go up' reads I've backwards, as in a down clue, and 'carried by' puts that inside the plural surname of Tony and Hilary Benn, both British Labour politicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Ben Nevis is the highest mountain in Britain, in the Scottish Highlands.

clue.text: Fellow in Soho about to gain employment in London building

parts.note: a fellow is a man

indicators.note: about here means scattered around, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: use means employment, as in putting something to use

explanation.surface: A man in Soho is about to find a job in a London building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges the letters of IN SOHO into SIONHO. Soho is a district of central London; the Mansion House is the Lord Mayor of London's official residence.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mansion House is a famous building in the City of London, home of the Lord Mayor.

clue.text: Notice flaw — get guidance

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
a vice is a flaw in character

explanation.surface: Spot a defect and seek help.
explanation.definitionFit: Advice is counsel or guidance given to someone.

clue.text: Sceptically philosophical in the manner of a German

parts.note: as means like or in the manner of
Immanuel Kant was a German philosopher

explanation.surface: A doubting philosopher acts like a German thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'philosophical' qualifies the German, telling the solver to think of Kant.
explanation.definitionFit: Askant means sideways or askance, with a doubtful, suspicious look.

clue.text: Record the times we are living in? One will get put off

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record

parts.words: the times we are living in
parts.note: our age is the present era, the times we live in

explanation.surface: Someone recording our present era expects one to be discouraged.
explanation.definitionFit: To discourage someone is to deter them, putting them off an action.

clue.text: Pair of horses very big, not half

indicators.note: not half means the second half of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: spanking is an informal word for very big or impressive

explanation.surface: Two horses that are not quite enormous.
explanation.walkthrough: SPANKING has eight letters; 'not half' removes the last four, KING.
explanation.definitionFit: A span is a pair of matched horses or draught animals harnessed together, chiefly an American usage.

clue.text: Foppish group

definitions.meaning: a faction or set of like-minded people

explanation.definitionFit: Camp means affectedly theatrical, and a camp is also a faction holding shared views.

clue.text: Latin is second of languages possibly for Romans?

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters may be arranged differently
second of means take the second letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Latin is perhaps the second language of the ancient Romans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second of' gives A from languages; 'possibly' mixes LATINIS plus A. 'Romans' looks like the ancient people but means the modern citizens of Rome, who are Italians.
explanation.definitionFit: Romans, as people from the city of Rome, are among the Italians.

clue.text: Vehicle taking time when reversing — one may help the driver

indicators.note: reversing means the whole run of letters is read backwards

parts.note: a van is a vehicle
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A van is reversing slowly, a manoeuvre where a driver needs help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing' turns VANTAS round as one unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A satellite navigation device gives drivers directions, so it helps the driver find the way.

clue.text: Meet Bond involved in a grave situation

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Meeting James Bond puts you in a serious predicament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave situation' seems to mean a crisis, but means literally placed in a grave.
explanation.definitionFit: Entombed means placed in a tomb, literally in a grave.

clue.text: People going sneakily around courts

indicators.note: around here means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: snoops are people who pry or sneak about

explanation.surface: Sneaky people are lurking around the law courts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'courts' looks like a noun for places of law, but it is the verb meaning woos.
explanation.definitionFit: To spoon is an old-fashioned word for behaving amorously, so it means courts or woos.
